title: Plural partitive of common -as/-äs words
summary: For these -as/-äs words, use strong consonants and replace -as/-äs with -aita/-äitä: vieras (“guest”) → vieraita.
objectives: Form the plural partitive in this bounded word family.

sections.title: Meaning and pattern
paragraphs: A case is a word form used for a grammatical job. The dictionary form is the form used to look up a word. The partitive has several uses; it does not always mean “some”. Here you practise forming the word, so no sentence construction is required.

In these selected -as/-äs words, replace -as with -aita or -äs with -äitä and use the strong consonants taught in the examples. A strong form can have pp or kk where the dictionary form has p or k. Learn the mm → mp and r → rk changes explicitly. This is a bounded family; other -as/-äs words can have different stems.
keyPoints: Learn each word with its pattern; a similar final letter does not guarantee the same stem.

steps: The word’s meaning stays connected to “guest”; its plural case form changes its grammatical use.
Change mm to mp and replace -as with -aita: hammas → hampaita.
The word’s meaning stays connected to “tooth”; its plural case form changes its grammatical use.
Change r to rk and replace -as with -aita: varas → varkaita.
The word’s meaning stays connected to “thief”; its plural case form changes its grammatical use.
Strengthen p to pp and replace -as with -aita: saapas → saappaita.
The word’s meaning stays connected to “boot”; its plural case form changes its grammatical use.
Strengthen p to pp and replace -as with -aita: opas → oppaita.
The word’s meaning stays connected to “guide”; its plural case form changes its grammatical use.
Strengthen k to kk and replace -as with -aita: rakas → rakkaita.
The word’s meaning stays connected to “dear”; its plural case form changes its grammatical use.
Strengthen k to kk and replace -as with -aita: rikas → rikkaita.
The word’s meaning stays connected to “rich”; its plural case form changes its grammatical use.
Strengthen k to kk and replace -äs with -äitä: älykäs → älykkäitä.
The word’s meaning stays connected to “intelligent”; its plural case form changes its grammatical use.

commonMistakes: Use the strong consonants in the plural.
Do not copy the unchanged-base singular -asta/-ästä ending.
